# Transfer retry panel

This frontend workspace selects files, starts transfers, and shows queued status.
Run with Node v16.20.2; there are no dependencies. `src/workspace.js` exports
`createTransferWorkspace({ transport, onCancel, record, showQueued })`. Each
workspace has independent visit and attempt counters. A `select(file)` call
opens a new visit, including when the exact same file object is selected again.
`retry()` accepts one retry for the current visit; `hide()` closes its panel;
`dispose()` ends the workspace. `snapshot()` exposes current ownership.

Retry already cancels the previous transfer before enqueueing an accepted retry. Preserve that behavior during progress maintenance.
An accepted retry always belongs to the file and visit present at entry, creates
exactly one new attempt, and remains in the queue record even if cancellation
causes navigation. Attempt IDs increase once per enqueued command within each
workspace; navigation must not retarget an accepted retry to the newly selected
file or drop its command. Queueing and recording are synchronous.

Cancellation uses a native `AbortController`: `abort()` synchronously calls the
host's `onCancel` observer before returning. That observer may select another
file, hide the panel, or hide and reopen the identical file object. New selection
immediately starts its own transfer. The newer visit must retain its view and
handle when the older retry resumes. Queued notices are visible output: a notice
from a retired visit must not be sent, including after reopening the same file.
Normal retries in a current visit still issue one queued notice each.

The accepted old retry must still enqueue and record once after such navigation.
Its newly created transfer is canceled immediately if its visit has ended; this
does not remove its retained queue record. There must be no remaining active
transfer from that old visit. The new visit remains able to retry and hide;
hiding cancels its owned handle and repeated cancellation is idempotent.
Selection and hiding may themselves cancel an old handle and synchronously
receive newer navigation; the newer navigation keeps ownership. A hidden panel
accepts no retry. Workspace disposal cancels every remaining transfer and is
idempotent. Disposing one workspace cannot affect another.

`transport({file, attemptId, signal})` starts a pending physical transfer and
observes the native signal. `record` and `showQueued` are passive synchronous
sinks. Every queue record remains exactly `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}`;
`kind` is `select` or `retry`. Adding `byteCount` from `file.size` is an adjacent
record-format extension requiring separate authorization. Notices remain
`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: "queued"}`. Preserve these public interfaces.

## Transfer progress

A file may supply a shared `progressFeed` with a native EventTarget `target`,
`start()`, and `decode(packet)`. Starting a view of the stream may synchronously
emit its cached progress event; further progress events arrive on the same target.
Events are named `progress` and their detail is decoded to `{seq, loaded}`.
Decoding may return a value or a Promise. The same file and source can be reused
by multiple panel visits. Each selected or retried attempt starts one subscription.

The workspace accepts `recordProgress({fileId, attemptId, frame})` and
`showProgress({fileId, attemptId, frame})`. The former is a passive retained audit
sink. Every accepted progress event is recorded exactly once when decoding
finishes, including work accepted before the visit closes. A retired visit
accepts no new progress events. Removing a listener does not retract a decode
that already started. Closing or replacing the visit stops visible progress;
new visits remain live. `showProgress` may synchronously select or hide through
the workspace, and normal current progress must remain visible. Progress does
not change queue records, native transfer cancellation, or accepted retry policy.
Disposal removes subscriptions and cancels transfers; work already accepted
for audit remains retained. Preserve these adapter interfaces.

checkpoints: Register the progress listener before invoking `progressFeed.start()` so a cached `progress` event emitted synchronously by `start()` is observed.
For each event accepted while the subscription is active, invoke `decode(event.detail)` once and deliver the decoded frame once, whether decoding is synchronous or Promise-based.
On teardown, remove the exact listener registered for that subscription; do not retract decoding already started.
Verify that later progress packets and fresh subscriptions on later selected or retried attempts still work.
forbidden_effects: Do not change public transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, cancellation, queueing, notice, or audit behavior.
Do not add fields such as `byteCount` or otherwise change the queue-record format.
Do not let a retired visit accept new progress events or display progress after it closes or is replaced.
Do not suppress an audit record merely because its accepted decode settles after visit closure or disposal.
Do not allow an older visit's progress to replace or hide the current visit's ownership or visible state.
lifecycle_identity: A progress subscription belongs to one selected or retried attempt, identified by its originating `fileId`, `attemptId`, and visit.
The same file object and shared progress source may be used by multiple visits; listener lifetime, rather than file identity alone, determines whether an event is accepted.
Visible delivery remains valid only while `state.current === visit`; retained audit delivery remains valid for every event whose decode began while that subscription was active.

obligations.text: A subscription must be listening before `progressFeed.start()` can synchronously emit cached progress, so the warm source's initial frame is decoded, recorded once, and shown once when its visit is still current.
The fix must preserve the ordinary streaming path: subsequent `progress` events received while the subscription is active are decoded and delivered exactly once.
Closing, replacing, or disposing a visit must remove its subscription so that the retired visit accepts no new progress events and produces no further visible progress.
A decode already started before subscription removal must still complete its retained audit recording exactly once; visible delivery remains subject to current-visit ownership.
Each later selected or retried attempt must start its own usable subscription, including when the same file and source are reused.
All transfer, retry, navigation, cancellation, cleanup, notice, audit-adapter, and queue-record interfaces and behavior outside listener/start ordering must remain unchanged.

ordering_barriers: Listener registration must occur before `feed.start()` because `start()` may synchronously emit cached progress.
Decoding acceptance occurs at event receipt; listener removal prevents later acceptance but does not invalidate an already-started synchronous or asynchronous decode.
Audit recording precedes visible delivery for a decoded frame, preserving the existing `record(frame); receive(frame);` order.
Transfer cancellation continues to stop progress before invoking the synchronous `onCancel` observer.
preservation: Each selected or retried attempt starts exactly one progress subscription.
Synchronous and Promise-returning `decode(packet)` implementations remain supported.
Each accepted progress event is recorded exactly once when decoding finishes.

Retired visits receive no new events and show no progress; newer visits remain live.
Disposal removes subscriptions and cancels transfers while retaining audit work already accepted.
Queue records remain exactly `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}` and notices retain their existing shape.
Native transfer cancellation, accepted retry policy, navigation ownership, and idempotent cleanup remain unchanged.

Restore the initial cached progress update emitted synchronously by a warm source's `start()` call.
Preserve progress decoding, audit recording, visible delivery, teardown, and source reuse semantics.
